text:
Samantha: FYI support escalation — multiple customers reporting intermittent timeouts and 5xxs on /v1/generate over the last 45m. Some report billing spikes due to client retries.
Raj: pulling logs for 3432109876 and 3432109877 now. any common request_id prefixes?
Samantha: support sent a handful of request_ids in the ticket: req_9a3f2, req_9a40b, req_9a55c. attaching one snippet: `504 gateway timeout, upstream read timed out`
Maya: can you paste the raw headers/payload for one of those? want to check seq_len and model selection.
Samantha: pasted in support thread: model=redwood-13b-v2, prompt len ~2k tokens, client timeout 30s, retries enabled (3x immediate).
Liam: interesting — model variant is cpu->gpu routed; sequence lengths might be triggering long KV-cache paths. seeing a small surge in EU region 10:42-11:10 UTC correlating with these ids.
Carlos: metrics show per-token latency spike on serving-pool-eu-2 between 10:30-11:05. Aggregated CPU on that pool hit 92%, queue depth increased.
Nora: any recent deploys to that pool?
deploy-bot: deploy completed: infra/serving-runtime v2.14.7 -> v2.15.0 at 10:25 UTC (rollout 30% eu-west).
Raj: ah — 30% rollout at exactly the start of the window. possible regression in batching or kernel selection.
Maya: quick repro plan: spin a small load test with prompt_len=2k using redwood-13b-v2, route to the canary pool. I'll run a 20qps test with the same timeout/retry behavior.
Liam: mitigation suggestions: 1) pause rollout to eu-west canary 2) enable automatic fallback on long tail to redwood-7b-optimized 3) temporarily increase circuit-breaker threshold for that pool to avoid bulk 5xx responses 4) post client guidance to add jittered backoff.
Samantha: support can push guidance to affected customers for client-side backoff + reduce retry to 1. I'll draft messaging.
Carlos: on the infra side I'll pause the rollout now and scale up the older pool by +2 nodes (warm) to absorb traffic. initiating now.
deploy-bot: action: rollout paused for infra/serving-runtime at 11:12 UTC.
Maya: ran a small repro against the canary: observed tail latencies >2s per token and occasional 504s when concurrent requests >12. root cause hypothesis: change in kernel selection that loses an optimized path for long sequences.
Raj: can we get the exact kernel/version diff between 2.14.7 and 2.15.0? I'll pull the build notes and CI kernel matrix.
Nora: I'll open an incident ticket with priority P1 and include customer list + SLAs impacted. support triage board updated.
Samantha: action items so far: 1) Carlos pause rollout & scale older pool (done) — owner Carlos — ETA 11:20 UTC 2) Support messaging to customers (Samantha) — draft in 10m 3) Repro & kernel diff (Maya/Raj) — report in 45m 4) Playbook for support to collect request_ids + client SDK guidance (Samantha/Nora) — deliverable in 30m
Carlos: scaled older pool, verifying traffic shift. queue depth dropping.
BillingBot: spike detected: customer acct acct-874 had a token-usage increase of 4.2x between 10:30-11:05 UTC — flagged for manual review.
Samantha: will pause auto-refunds until we confirm cause. notifying CS to hold escalation.
Raj: preliminary kernel diff: we changed attention tiling heuristics that alter kernel choice for seq_len > 1024 on some GPUs. that maps to the observed window. submitting PR to revert heuristic in canary.
Maya: repro run against reverted binary shows stable tail latencies and no 504 reproduction under identical load.
Liam: recommend staged rollback on canary to previous runtime version, then monitor 30m before progressive rollout.
Nora: scheduling postmortem sync for 2pm UTC today; will capture timeline, impact, and customer outreach plan.
Samantha: final note for support: collect these fields for any future reports: request_id, model, seq_len, region, client_retry_settings, timestamp. I'll add a short checklist doc and paste link here.
Samantha: quick checklist draft: `1) ask for request_id(s) 2) ask for full headers+payload 3) ask whether client retries were enabled 4) ask for region/model 5) advise temporary reduce retries & enable jittered exponential backoff`
Carlos: rollback completed to v2.14.7 on canary at 11:45 UTC, monitoring.
deploy-bot: rollback completed: infra/serving-runtime -> v2.14.7 at 11:45 UTC (canary: 100% reverted).
Liam: monitoring graphs look back to normal, tail p95 latency down to baseline. leaving alerting on for next 2 hours.
Samantha: thanks everyone. Support will follow up with the affected customers with apology + guidance and hold any refunds until we complete impact review.
Nora: postmortem notes assigned — I'll compile timeline, cause (kernel heuristic regression), mitigation (rollback + scaling), action items (improve canary gating, add auto-diff alerts for kernel changes, enhance billing anomaly detection), owners and due dates. meeting invite sent. :spiral_note_pad:
